title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): X is a topological surface and 𝒢 a discrete group acting on it. G is a normal subgroup of 𝒢 acting properly on X. Each stabilizer G_x acts faithfully near x and preserves the local orientation, so it is finite cyclic and acts by rotations. Put Y = X/G, f: X→Y, and ℋ = 𝒢/G, which acts on Y.

X^! is a discrete 𝒢-stable subset of X containing every point with nontrivial stabilizer. d_X: X^!→ℕ is a 𝒢-invariant 'signature' (the allowed ramification index at each marked point). The induced signature on Y^! = X^!/G is d_Y(f(x)) = |G_x|·d_X(x).

Rev(X,d_X,𝒢) is the category of 𝒢-equivariant ramified coverings of X, étale off X^!, whose ramification at a ∈ X^! is subordinate to (divides) d_X(a). Rev(Y,d_Y,ℋ) is the analogous category on Y.

The page asserts four things:
(a) For X' in Rev(X,d_X,𝒢), the quotient X'/G, with its induced ℋ-action over Y, lies in Rev(Y,d_Y,ℋ).
(b) This gives a functor Rev(X,d_X,𝒢) → Rev(Y,d_Y,ℋ). The equation number is read as (9) in the transcription, probably (19).
(c) This functor is an equivalence of categories.
(d) A quasi-inverse is the 'normalized' pullback: Y' ↦ the normalization of X ×_Y Y', with its 𝒢-action.

Reductions ('OPS' = on peut supposer):
- One may assume d_X > 0, equivalently d_Y > 0. Points with d = 0 (no relation on the local loop, i.e. arbitrary or infinite ramification) are simply removed: S from X and T = S/G from Y.
- One may assume that d_X(x) = 1 forces G_x ≠ 1. Points with d_X = 1 and trivial stabilizer impose no condition, so they can be dropped from X^!.

The key case: d_X ≡ 1 on X^! = {x : G_x ≠ 1}. Then Rev(X,d_X,𝒢) = Rev(X,𝒢), the 𝒢-equivariant étale coverings of X with no ramification data (equation (10), probably (20)). The equivalence then identifies the category of orbifold coverings of Y, with cone indices d_Y(y) = |G_x|, with the 𝒢-equivariant unramified coverings of X.

Purpose: this is the categorical input for the next page's corollary. There one gets π_1((X,d_X,𝒢),x) ≅ π_1((Y,d_Y,ℋ),y), made explicit by pairs (γ, path class from x to γ^{-1}x modulo the normal subgroup generated by λ_a^{d_X(a)}). It serves the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets': computing orbifold fundamental groups of quotient surfaces (moduli of curves, Teichmüller-type situations) as extensions by the discrete group.
errors: No mathematical error. Correctness of (c) needs the stated hypotheses: G acts properly and stabilizers act faithfully and orientation-preservingly. Under these the local model is the quotient of a disc by a cyclic rotation group, and the multiplicativity d_Y = |G_x|·d_X(x) is exactly right.
The convention d = 0 meaning 'no relation' (puncture) is implicit. The reduction 'remove S' is consistent with it.

ideas.what: Equivalence between 𝒢-equivariant ramified coverings of X with signature d_X and ℋ-equivariant ramified coverings of Y = X/G with signature d_Y = |G_x|·d_X, via quotient by G, with quasi-inverse given by normalized pullback
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold coverings of a good 2-orbifold / coverings of the quotient stack [X/G] versus root stacks; Abhyankar-type descent of tame coverings along a Galois quotient
ideas.usually_credited_to: Orbifold version: Thurston (late 1970s), building on Fox (branched coverings) and Bundgaard–Nielsen/Fenchel; algebraic tame version: Grothendieck–Murre and SGA1 Exp. XIII (Abhyankar's lemma)
ideas.where_published: Closely related material is in SGA1 (Exp. V, XIII) and in Grothendieck–Murre, Lecture Notes in Math. 208 (1971). The surface/'signature' formulation resembles La Longue Marche (1981) but is unsure there.

ideas.what: Normalizing the signature: discard points with d = 0 (punctures) and points with d = 1 and trivial stabilizer; the case d_X ≡ 1 on the fixed-point locus reduces equivariant coverings to unramified ones
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold structure on Y induced by a proper cyclic-stabilizer action; equivariant fundamental group as orbifold fundamental group

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, correct but standard statement: quotient by a properly acting normal subgroup gives an equivalence of equivariant ramified coverings with multiplied signatures. It is well known as orbifold covering theory and as tame descent (SGA1/Grothendieck–Murre). It is a lemma toward an explicit isomorphism of orbifold fundamental groups, with nothing beyond the literature.
transcription_corrections: Equation numbers: the image appears to read '(19)' for the functor and '(20)' for Rev(X,d_X,𝒢)=Rev(X,𝒢). This fits the next page's '(21)'; the transcription has (9) and (10).
In 'Rev({Y}, d_Y, ℋ) peut donc', the brace is a stray mark; it should read Rev(Y, d_Y, ℋ).
The interlinear correction reads: 'OPS d_X(x)=1 ⇒ [G_x]≠1 (sinon, remplacer X^! par X^!∖S, S={x∈X^! | d_X(x)=1, [G_x]=1})'.
